topic: Full-scale honest evaluation of the trigger2 diagnostic model+shell against 852 real never-seen HOLDOUT_FROZEN rows (up to 60/family, all 16 trained families), run live in the claylab sandbox
scope: 2534 total HOLDOUT_FROZEN rows exist across the 16 trained B0-B6 files; running literally all of them on CPU would take ~105 minutes. Ran a stratified sample instead: every real HOLDOUT_FROZEN row up to a cap of 60/family (852 rows total, full coverage of every family, none capped below its true size except B0_READ at 12/12, B2_STALE at 36/36, B6_CLAUDE_HANDOFF at 48/48, B6_DB_VS_SIM at 36/36 which have fewer than 60 holdout rows total -- those are fully exhaustive, not sampled).
raw_data: SHELL_WRAPPER_LARGE_852_RESULTS_20260827.jsonl in this packet directory -- one real generation + shell-validation result per line, all 852.

B0_READ_BASELINE.note: at chance for a 3-way ALLOW/DENY/ABSTAIN task -- not really learned

B1_TRAIN_BALANCED_2ORDER.note: sometimes produces a real atom, never the right one

B2_PRIOR_OVERRIDE.note: CONFIRMED systematic bug at full scale: always answers with a codebook KEY (ALLOW/DENY/ABSTAIN) instead of the VALUE it maps to -- 60/60, not a sampling artifact

B3_MULTI_HOP_DEREF.note: CONFIRMED total collapse at full scale -- every single generation derailed

B4_CAPACITY_INTERFERENCE.note: CONFIRMED total collapse -- consistently echoes the queried entity name instead of its mapped atom

B5_VARIABLE_N_EQUIVARIANCE.note: CONFIRMED total collapse -- consistently emits a bare single letter instead of the ordinal atom

B6_CLAUDE_HANDOFF_REENTRY.note: strongest family in the whole curriculum

the_real_finding_not_just_the_number: The result is sharply BIMODAL, not uniformly mediocre. Two clean groups: (A) direct-classification/system-integration families -- all of B6 (Claude-handoff, DB-vs-sim, GWT x3, Hyperposition), plus B0_WRITE and B2_STALE_BINDING_REJECTION -- validate at ~100% and score 33-88% correct, meaningfully to strongly above chance on every one. (B) indirection/binding/multi-step families -- B1 (arbitrary binding), B2_MID_EPISODE_REMAP, B2_PRIOR_OVERRIDE, both B3 variants (multi-hop dereference), B4 (capacity/interference), B5 (variable-N equivariance) -- are at or near 0% correct, several at literal 0% shell-validation (every single generation rejected). This is coherent, not noise: group (B) is exactly the set of families whose whole research point was teaching NEW indirection/binding mechanics the base model has no pretrained prior for, versus group (A) which is closer to direct in-context classification given an already-present answer. One epoch of light LoRA on 9544 rows taught the easier half convincingly and did not move the harder half off its pretrained priors at all.
confirmed_bugs_grounded_in_full_data: B2_PRIOR_OVERRIDE codebook-key-leak: 60/60 rows, always answers with the ALLOW/DENY/ABSTAIN key instead of the ABI_ACCEPTED_ORDINAL value it maps to. Root cause hypothesis (same shape as the earlier B3 finding): the prompt's own surface text contains those exact words as codebook keys, and the model echoes a nearby key instead of performing the lookup.

B3 (both variants) total code-derailment collapse: 120/120 rows, 0 validated. Confirms the earlier smaller-sample finding (pointer/dereference/CHAIN vocabulary triggers a strong pretrained code-completion prior) at full statistical confidence, not an artifact of a small sample.

B4 entity-echo and B5 bare-letter collapse: 120/120 rows, 0 validated. Both are format failures, not vocabulary/reasoning failures per se -- the model is engaging with the task (echoing a real entity name from the prompt, or picking a plausible-looking short answer) but never emitting the required ABI_ACCEPTED_ORDINAL:NN wrapper.
